transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm really struggling with overwhelming, uncontrollable urges to constantly wash my hands and clean everything around me. It has gotten to the point where it's taking over my entire daily life, and I just can't seem to stop.
When you feel the urge to wash or clean, what specific thoughts, fears, or images are going through your mind?

I have this intense, overwhelming fear of germs and contamination, and I constantly feel like everything I touch is filthy. I get terrified that if I don't wash my hands or clean immediately, the dirt will spread and make me or others sick. Washing is the only way I can temporarily get rid of that dirty, anxious feeling.
Aside from your concerns about germs and cleaning, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday life areas, such as your finances, work, or family?

No, I don't really worry about things like my finances or work. Almost all of my anxiety and focus are centered on germs, contamination, and keeping things clean. It's those thoughts that take up all my energy.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Based on the patient's report, their anxiety and worry are entirely focused on contamination and cleaning compulsions, and they deny generalized worry about everyday life areas like finances, work, or family. This rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder, leaving Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder as the sole and final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with intrusive, distressing thoughts regarding contamination and germs (obsessions) alongside repetitive, ritualistic handwashing and cleaning behaviors (compulsions) performed to alleviate the resulting anxiety. These symptoms cause significant impairment in daily functioning and are not driven by generalized worries about everyday life, supporting a diagnosis of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
